extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A synthetic texture dataset containing 246,285 high-quality, diverse texture images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts and a three-stage refinement process.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated using text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion) with texture-specific prompts. The process involved three steps: (1) producing texture-specific prompts using artistically-informed descriptors across texture classes, (2) using these prompts as inputs to adapted Stable Diffusion model pipelines, and (3) performing a three-stage refinement process consisting of frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring to filter images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of texture images generated by Stable Diffusion models from texture-specific prompts. The prompts were constructed using combinations of artistically-informed descriptors applied across 56 texture classes, resulting in 246,285 texture images before refinement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation conducted on texture quality and representativeness at each stage of refinement process. Evaluators assessed whether images were high-quality and representative of real textures.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation showed 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness overall, with each stage of refinement process positively contributing to success
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion text-to-image model for image generation; CLIP for scoring alignment between images and prompts; Inception model for quality and diversity assessment; frequency analysis via Fourier transforms for object removal; patch variance filtering for homogeneity removal
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is generated using text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion) which face unique challenges including safety filter sensitivity to texture data. Traditional texture synthesis methods are example-based and lack textual descriptions, making it challenging to control for specific texture characteristics or align textures with semantic labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports texture-based research tasks including understanding high-level features models learn, constructing texture-object associations, analyzing texture bias in models, creating adversarial examples, and measuring texture bias through Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric for object classification models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged by NSFW safety filter were regenerated to ensure consistent number of images per prompt. Five images were generated per prompt, resulting in 483,840 images before refinement. Images flagged as NSFW were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three-stage refinement process applied to filter generated images: (1) Frequency filtering using Fourier transforms to remove object-like images by retaining top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values, applied in balanced manner across texture classes; (2) Patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images; (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure alignment with prompts. Final dataset contains 246,285 images from initial 483,840 images.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our approach takes place in three steps. First, we produce texture-specific prompts to serve as the basis for our texture generation, where we apply combinations of artistically-informed descriptors across a wide range of texture classes to enable controlled diversity of textures. Second, we use our constructed prompts as inputs to Stable Diffusion model pipelines, which we adapt based on unique challenges we uncover that arise from safety filters sensitivity to texture data, to produce the corresponding texture images. Finally, to yield higher-quality and more texture-like images, we perform a three stage refinement process consisting of frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring to filter down the images.
